methodological_questions: effect of preceding drive by a teammate on pick and roll points per possession

historical_evidence.finding: Per‑lag analysis shows that a single prior possession improves predictive accuracy of next‑possession outcome; lag‑1 effect is strongest and plateaus after 3 possessions.
Play‑type PPP across playoff series buckets shows stable or improving DRIVE PPP; no clear pattern for pick and roll PPP but indicates selection biases in series data.
Within‑game DRIVE efficiency increases over time, not decreases; demonstrates that raw play‑type effects can be confounded by game‑time evolution.

evidence_establishes: Sequential possession effects exist; lag‑1 prior possession can influence next‑possession outcome.
There is substantial data on play‑type PPP across seasons and series, but no published test of drive‑preceded pick‑and‑roll PPP.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a teammate drive specifically raises pick‑and‑roll PPP compared to other preceding plays.
Causal direction of the effect without controlling for teammate identity and game context.
own_inferences: The data set contains millions of possessions, so statistical power will be adequate if proper controls are applied.
Defining a ‘preceded by drive’ event requires parsing possession sequences and ensuring they belong to the same teammate.
uncertainties: Exact operational definition of a drive preceding a pick‑and‑roll on the same possession or following possession.
Potential mislabeling or ambiguity in play‑type tags in the graph database.

historical_effect.explanation: Historical records do not directly address the question, so the decision is unchanged.

blocking_constraints.text: Teammate identity, game state, and defense can confound the drive→PNR relationship.
Play‑type labels are derived from automated algorithms and may contain classification error.

prior_work.summary: Prior studies demonstrate sequential effects and play‑type PPP patterns but none test drive‑preceded pick‑and‑roll PPP.

risks.text: Teammate identity and game context may bias the observed relationship.
Automated play‑type labeling may misclassify drives or pick‑and‑rolls.
While overall sample is large, the specific subset of drive→PNR sequences may be smaller.

design.estimand: Difference in pick‑and‑roll PPP when preceded by a teammate drive versus any other preceding play.
design.sample: All pick‑and‑roll possessions with a teammate drive in the immediately preceding possession, matched to pick‑and‑roll possessions with other preceding plays.
design.power: High – n>10,000 pick‑and‑roll possessions in the drive‑preceded group; power >0.8 for d≈0.1.
design.controls: Teammate identity, opponent defense rating, game state (score margin, period), possession context (home/away, team strength).
design.falsification: Test the same model with non‑teammate drives preceding pick‑and‑roll and with reverse sequencing (PNR followed by drive).
design.multiplicity: Adjust for multiple play‑type comparisons using Holm‑Bonferroni; pre‑register primary hypothesis.
design.decision_rule: Reject null if p<0.01 after adjustment; otherwise report effect size with 95% CI.
design.data_version: NBA 2022‑23 through 2025‑26 regular season and playoffs, play‑by‑play derived possession graph.
